```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(restriktor)
library(ggplot2)
results_file <- "coverage_evSyn_CI_results.rds"
```

# Aim

`evSyn_CI()` gives confidence intervals (CIs) for the pooled (final) results of a GORICA
evidence synthesis: the pooled GORICA values, the differences in pooled GORICA values, the
pooled GORICA weights, and the ratios of pooled GORICA weights. This simulation study
evaluates the coverage of these CIs for the two available approaches:

* `method = "boot"` (default): parametric bootstrap, drawing per study from N(estimates, VCOV),
  independently over the studies, and taking percentiles of the pooled quantities;
* `method = "delta"`: normal-based (delta-method) CIs, with the covariance matrix of the pooled
  log-likelihood values as the sum of the study-specific ones (and the CIs of the weights on the
  logit scale).

# Design

## Data-generating model

Each study estimates three (standardized) parameters, say three group means with unit variance
and $n$ observations per group. The estimates of study $s$ are drawn as
$\hat\theta_s \sim N(\theta, V)$, with $V = \mathrm{diag}(1/n, 1/n, 1/n)$; this is exactly the
(asymptotic) model underlying the GORICA. The studies are independent and have the same true
parameters $\theta$ (no heterogeneity).

## Hypotheses

Two sets of hypotheses are evaluated:

* **Set A**: $H_1: \theta_1 > \theta_2 > \theta_3$ and $H_2: \theta_1 > \theta_2 = \theta_3$,
  with the unconstrained hypothesis as failsafe (the default for more than one hypothesis);
* **Set B**: $H_1: \theta_1 > \theta_2 > \theta_3$ versus its complement
  (the default for one hypothesis).

## Conditions

```{r conditions}
thetas <- list(
  inside   = c(b1 = 0.4, b2 = 0.2, b3 = 0.0),  # in H1, not in H2
  boundary = c(b1 = 0.2, b2 = 0.0, b3 = 0.0),  # on the boundary of H1 and in H2: overlap
  outside  = c(b1 = 0.0, b2 = 0.2, b3 = 0.4),  # in the opposite order
  null     = c(b1 = 0.0, b2 = 0.0, b3 = 0.0)   # all equal
)
hypo_sets <- list(
  A = list(H1 = "b1 > b2 > b3", H2 = "b1 > b2 = b3"),  # failsafe: unconstrained
  B = list(H1 = "b1 > b2 > b3")                        # failsafe: complement
)
conditions <- expand.grid(theta = names(thetas), n = c(25, 100), S = c(3, 10),
                          type_ev = c("added", "equal"), hypo_set = names(hypo_sets),
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# The equal-evidence approach is only evaluated for set A (for the differences and
# ratios, it gives the same CIs as the added-evidence approach up to a constant).
conditions <- conditions[!(conditions$hypo_set == "B" & conditions$type_ev == "equal"), ]
rownames(conditions) <- NULL
nrow(conditions)
```

This gives `r nrow(conditions)` conditions: 4 true parameter vectors $\times$ 2 sample sizes per
group ($n$ = 25, 100) $\times$ 2 numbers of studies ($S$ = 3, 10) $\times$ the evidence-synthesis
approach (added; equal for set A) $\times$ 2 sets of hypotheses. Each condition is replicated
$R$ = `r params$R` times, with $B$ = `r params$B` bootstrap draws per study. With $R$ = `r params$R`,
the Monte Carlo standard error of an estimated coverage of .95 is
`r round(sqrt(.95 * .05 / params$R), 3)`, so estimated coverages in between
`r round(.95 - 2 * sqrt(.95 * .05 / params$R), 3)` and `r round(.95 + 2 * sqrt(.95 * .05 / params$R), 3)`
are in line with a coverage of .95.

## Estimand

As for `goric_CI()`, the population counterparts of the GORICA values are their *expected* values,
$E[\mathrm{GORICA}_m] = \log|2\pi V| + E[D_m] + 2\,PT_m$, with $D_m$ the squared Mahalanobis
distance of the estimates to $H_m$ and $PT_m$ the (fixed) penalty. For the pooled results
(equal prior weights and equal study weights):

* added: $E[\mathrm{GORICA}^{pool}_m] = S \cdot E[\mathrm{GORICA}_m]$;
* equal: $E[\mathrm{GORICA}^{pool}_m] = S \cdot (E[\mathrm{GORICA}_m] - 2\,PT_m) + 2\,PT_m$
  (log-likelihoods summed, penalty averaged).

The target values of the differences, the weights, and the ratios of weights follow from these
expected pooled values. The expected values are obtained by Monte Carlo at the true parameters
(`r format(params$nsim_target, big.mark = ",")` draws).

```{r targets-functions}
# Expected GORICA values (per hypothesis) for one study with estimates ~ N(theta, V)
expected_IC <- function(theta, V, hyps, nsim) {
  g <- goric(theta, VCOV = V, hypotheses = hyps)   # object at the true parameters
  models <- as.character(g$result$model)
  draws <- restriktor:::goric_CI_boot(g, models, B = nsim)
  list(EIC = colMeans(draws), PT = g$result$penalty)
}

# Target values for the pooled results (equal priors, equal study weights)
pooled_targets <- function(E, S, type_ev, pf = 2) {
  EIC <- if (type_ev == "added") S * E$EIC else S * (E$EIC - pf * E$PT) + pf * E$PT
  eta <- -EIC / 2
  w <- exp(eta - max(eta)); w <- w / sum(w)
  list(IC = EIC, weights = w,
       diff  = outer(EIC, EIC, "-"),          # [m, k] = IC_m - IC_k
       ratio = exp(outer(eta, eta, "-")))     # [m, k] = w_m / w_k
}
```

## One replication

For each replication, $S$ studies are generated, `evSyn()` is run, and the CIs of both methods are
computed. For each quantity, it is recorded whether the CI contains the target value, whether the CI
is missing (the delta method gives no CI for a difference/ratio when the two hypotheses have the same
order-restricted MLEs in *all* studies), and the width of the CI (on the log scale for ratios).

```{r one-rep}
one_rep <- function(cond, tg, B) {
  theta <- thetas[[cond$theta]]; hyps <- hypo_sets[[cond$hypo_set]]
  n <- cond$n; S <- cond$S
  V <- diag(1 / n, 3)
  est <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setNames(theta + rnorm(3, 0, sqrt(1 / n)), names(theta)))
  r <- suppressMessages(evSyn(est, VCOV = rep(list(V), S), hypotheses = hyps, type_ev = cond$type_ev))
  out <- list()
  for (method in c("boot", "delta")) {
    ci <- suppressMessages(evSyn_CI(r, method = method, B = B))
    M <- nrow(ci$IC)
    # ratios and differences: hypothesis 1 (H1) versus the others
    for (k in 2:M) {
      j <- which(ci$ratio_weights$model == ci$IC$model[1] & ci$ratio_weights$vs == ci$IC$model[k])
      lo <- ci$ratio_weights$lower[j]; up <- ci$ratio_weights$upper[j]; tt <- tg$ratio[1, k]
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(method = method, quantity = "ratio",
        comparison = paste0("H1 vs. ", c("H2", "failsafe")[min(k - 1, 2)][1]),
        covered = !is.na(lo) && lo <= tt && tt <= up, missing = is.na(lo),
        width = if (is.na(lo)) NA else log(up) - log(lo))
      lo <- ci$difference$lower[j]; up <- ci$difference$upper[j]; tt <- tg$diff[1, k]
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(method = method, quantity = "difference",
        comparison = paste0("H1 vs. ", c("H2", "failsafe")[min(k - 1, 2)][1]),
        covered = !is.na(lo) && lo <= tt && tt <= up, missing = is.na(lo),
        width = if (is.na(lo)) NA else up - lo)
    }
    # weight of H1
    lo <- ci$weights$lower[1]; up <- ci$weights$upper[1]; tt <- tg$weights[1]
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(method = method, quantity = "weight", comparison = "H1",
      covered = !is.na(lo) && lo <= tt && tt <= up, missing = is.na(lo),
      width = if (is.na(lo)) NA else up - lo)
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, out)
  # in set B, the second hypothesis is the failsafe (complement)
  if (cond$hypo_set == "B") out$comparison[out$comparison == "H1 vs. H2"] <- "H1 vs. failsafe"
  out
}
```

## Running the simulation

The simulation is run in parallel over the replications (with `future.apply`). It is only run
when the parameter `run_simulation` is `TRUE`; otherwise, the saved results are used.

```{r run, eval = params$run_simulation}
library(future.apply)
plan(multisession, workers = params$workers)
set.seed(2026)
res <- vector("list", nrow(conditions))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(conditions))) {
  cond <- conditions[i, ]
  V <- diag(1 / cond$n, 3)
  E <- expected_IC(thetas[[cond$theta]], V, hypo_sets[[cond$hypo_set]], nsim = params$nsim_target)
  tg <- pooled_targets(E, cond$S, cond$type_ev)
  reps <- future_lapply(seq_len(params$R), function(r) one_rep(cond, tg, params$B),
                        future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = "restriktor",
                        future.globals = list(one_rep = one_rep, cond = cond, tg = tg,
                                              thetas = thetas, hypo_sets = hypo_sets, params = params))
  reps <- do.call(rbind, reps)
  res[[i]] <- cbind(cond[rep(1, nrow(reps)), , drop = FALSE], reps, row.names = NULL)
}
plan(sequential)
res <- do.call(rbind, res)
saveRDS(list(res = res, params = params, sessionInfo = sessionInfo()), results_file)
```

# Results

```{r load}
sim <- readRDS(results_file)
res <- sim$res
summ <- aggregate(cbind(coverage = covered, missing = missing) ~ theta + n + S + type_ev +
                    hypo_set + method + quantity + comparison, data = res, FUN = mean)
wid <- aggregate(width ~ theta + n + S + type_ev + hypo_set + method + quantity + comparison,
                 data = res, FUN = median)
names(wid)[names(wid) == "width"] <- "median_width"
summ <- merge(summ, wid, all.x = TRUE)
summ$theta <- factor(summ$theta, levels = names(thetas))
mcse <- sqrt(.95 * .05 / sim$params$R)
```

The results are based on R = `r sim$params$R` replications per condition and B = `r sim$params$B`
bootstrap draws per study. The gray band in the figures denotes .95 $\pm$ 2 Monte Carlo standard errors.
A CI that is missing (delta method, see above) is counted as not covering the target value.

## Ratios of GORICA weights

```{r fig-ratio, fig.height = 7}
plot_cov <- function(d, title) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = theta, y = coverage, colour = method, shape = factor(S))) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = .95 - 2 * mcse, ymax = .95 + 2 * mcse,
             alpha = .25, fill = "gray60") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .95, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = .5)) +
    facet_grid(comparison + hypo_set ~ type_ev + n, labeller = label_both) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(.5, min(d$coverage)), 1)) +
    labs(x = "True parameters", y = "Coverage", shape = "S", colour = "Method", title = title) +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}
plot_cov(subset(summ, quantity == "ratio"), "Coverage of the CIs of the ratios of pooled GORICA weights")
```

## Differences in GORICA values

```{r fig-diff, fig.height = 7}
plot_cov(subset(summ, quantity == "difference"), "Coverage of the CIs of the differences in pooled GORICA values")
```

## GORICA weight of H1

```{r fig-weight, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_cov(subset(summ, quantity == "weight"), "Coverage of the CIs of the pooled GORICA weight of H1")
```

# Diagnostics: degenerate CIs

The coverage is evaluated strictly (the target value must lie in the CI). When both hypotheses 
have the same order-restricted MLEs in (nearly) all studies, the sampling distribution of their 
difference is (nearly) a point mass, and so is its CI; the expected value then differs from that 
point by a negligible amount, which a strict evaluation counts as non-coverage. For the condition 
with the lowest coverage for H1 versus H2 with $S$ = 3 (parameters in the opposite order, $n$ = 100), 
the CIs were recomputed while storing their bounds, and the coverage was also evaluated with a small 
tolerance (0.1 on the scale of the difference in GORICA values, i.e., about 5\% on the scale of the 
ratio of weights):

```{r diag-code, eval = FALSE}
# Diagnostic for the evSyn_CI() condition with a low (strict) coverage for H1 versus H2
# (parameters in the opposite order, S = 3, n = 100): strict versus tolerant coverage and degenerate CIs.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(restriktor))
set.seed(5)
R <- 200; B <- 500; tol <- 0.1; S <- 3; n <- 100
th <- c(b1 = 0, b2 = .2, b3 = .4); V <- diag(1 / n, 3)
H <- list(H1 = "b1 > b2 > b3", H2 = "b1 > b2 = b3")
g0 <- goric(th, VCOV = V, hypotheses = H)
EIC <- colMeans(restriktor:::goric_CI_boot(g0, as.character(g0$result$model), B = 2e5))
target <- S * (EIC[1] - EIC[2])
b <- t(replicate(R, {
  est <- lapply(1:S, function(s) setNames(th + rnorm(3, 0, sqrt(1 / n)), names(th)))
  ci <- evSyn_CI(suppressMessages(evSyn(est, VCOV = rep(list(V), S), hypotheses = H)), B = B)$difference
  j <- which(ci$model == "H1" & ci$vs == "H2"); c(ci$lower[j], ci$upper[j])
}))
d <- data.frame(S = S, n = n, comparison = "H1 vs. H2", theta = "outside", target = target,
                strict = mean(b[, 1] <= target & target <= b[, 2]),
                tolerant = mean(b[, 1] - tol <= target & target <= b[, 2] + tol),
                degenerate = mean(b[, 2] - b[, 1] < 1e-6))
print(d, row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(d, "diag_evSyn_CI.rds")
```

```{r diag-results}
knitr::kable(readRDS("diag_evSyn_CI.rds"), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

So, this low (strict) coverage is an artifact of degenerate (point) CIs: with the tolerance, the 
coverage is 1. The undercoverage for the best hypothesis versus the failsafe with $S$ = 10 is not 
such an artifact: it is removed by centering the bootstrap draws (see the next section).

# A possible improvement: centering the bootstrap

The undercoverage of the bootstrap with $S$ = 10 studies has a clear cause. For a difference in 
GORICA values $T$, the bootstrap draws $T^*$ (around the estimates) are shifted relative to the 
sampling distribution of $T$ (around the true parameters): in a study, the projection of a 
bootstrap draw adds, on average, roughly the number of active restrictions to $D_m$ 
(see also `?goric_CI`). In one study, this shift is small relative to the spread of $T$. In the 
pooled results, however, the shifts add up over the studies (they grow with $S$), whereas the spread 
grows with $\sqrt{S}$ only. Hence, the percentile CI is increasingly shifted with more studies.

A natural correction is to center the bootstrap draws: estimate the shift by 
$\bar{T}^* - T_{obs}$ and remove it. Two versions were evaluated in a smaller simulation (the 
pooled difference H1 versus the failsafe, added evidence, $n$ = 25, R = 250, B = 500), using the 
same bootstrap draws for all three versions:

* `percentile`: the current CI, the percentiles of $T^*$;
* `centered_perc`: $T_{obs} + [q_{.025}, q_{.975}]$ of $Z = T^* - \bar{T}^*$;
* `centered_basic`: $T_{obs} - [q_{.975}, q_{.025}]$ of $Z = T^* - \bar{T}^*$ (reversed, as in the 
  basic bootstrap).

```{r proto-code, eval = FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(restriktor))
set.seed(11)
R <- 250; B <- 500
thetas <- list(null = c(b1 = 0, b2 = 0, b3 = 0), boundary = c(b1 = .2, b2 = 0, b3 = 0),
               outside = c(b1 = 0, b2 = .2, b3 = .4), inside = c(b1 = .4, b2 = .2, b3 = 0))
hs <- list(A = list(H1 = "b1 > b2 > b3", H2 = "b1 > b2 = b3"), B = list(H1 = "b1 > b2 > b3"))
out <- list()
for (hn in names(hs)) for (tn in names(thetas)) for (S in c(3, 10)) {
  n <- 25; V <- diag(1 / n, 3); th <- thetas[[tn]]
  g0 <- goric(th, VCOV = V, hypotheses = hs[[hn]]); mods <- as.character(g0$result$model); M <- length(mods)
  EIC <- colMeans(restriktor:::goric_CI_boot(g0, mods, B = 1e5))
  target <- S * (EIC[1] - EIC[M])                         # pooled difference H1 vs failsafe (added)
  cov <- matrix(NA, R, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("percentile", "centered_perc", "centered_basic")))
  for (r in 1:R) {
    Tobs <- 0; Tb <- 0
    for (s in 1:S) {
      g <- goric(th + rnorm(3, 0, sqrt(1 / n)), VCOV = V, hypotheses = hs[[hn]])
      ICb <- restriktor:::goric_CI_boot(g, mods, B = B)
      Tobs <- Tobs + (g$result$gorica[1] - g$result$gorica[M])
      Tb <- Tb + (ICb[, 1] - ICb[, M])
    }
    q <- quantile(Tb, c(.025, .975)); Z <- Tb - mean(Tb)
    qz <- quantile(Z, c(.025, .975))
    cov[r, ] <- c(q[1] <= target & target <= q[2],
                  Tobs + qz[1] <= target & target <= Tobs + qz[2],
                  Tobs - qz[2] <= target & target <= Tobs - qz[1])
  }
  out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(set = hn, theta = tn, S = S, t(colMeans(cov)))
  print(tail(out, 1)[[1]], row.names = FALSE)
}
saveRDS(do.call(rbind, out), "proto_centered.rds")
```

```{r proto-results}
proto <- readRDS("proto_centered.rds")
knitr::kable(proto, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Coverage of the CI of the pooled difference H1 versus the failsafe")
```

Centering removes the undercoverage with $S$ = 10 (coverage .96 to 1.00), but neither centered 
version is uniformly good: the centered percentile version is conservative in nearly all conditions 
(coverage close to 1, so the CIs are too wide), and the centered basic version undercovers somewhat 
with $S$ = 3 in some conditions (.89 to .92). The reason is that, near the boundaries of the 
hypotheses, the shift (and the shape of the distribution) depends on where the true parameters 
are, so it is not estimated exactly by the shift at the estimates. This is the same reason why 
`goric_CI()` uses an inversion of the sampling distribution where possible.

# Conclusions

```{r conclusions-data, include = FALSE}
cov_rng <- function(m, q) {
  d <- subset(summ, method == m & quantity == q)
  sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(d$coverage), max(d$coverage))
}
```

The coverages (ranges over all conditions) are:

* ratios of weights: bootstrap `r cov_rng("boot", "ratio")`; delta method `r cov_rng("delta", "ratio")`;
* differences in GORICA values: bootstrap `r cov_rng("boot", "difference")`; delta method `r cov_rng("delta", "difference")`;
* weight of H1: bootstrap `r cov_rng("boot", "weight")`; delta method `r cov_rng("delta", "weight")`.

**Bootstrap (`method = "boot"`, the default).** With $S$ = 3 studies, the coverage is close to 
.95 or somewhat conservative in nearly all conditions (ratios of weights: .93 to 1.00 per condition), 
with one exception: H1 versus H2 when the parameters are in the opposite order and $n$ = 100 (.66), 
which is an artifact of degenerate (point) CIs (with a small tolerance, the coverage is 1; see 
"Diagnostics"). 
With $S$ = 10 studies, the CIs undercover for the best hypothesis versus the failsafe (the 
unconstrained hypothesis or the complement): about .74 to .78 when all parameters are equal, .79 to 
.92 on the boundary of H1, .79 to .87 when the parameters are in the opposite order, and .83 to .96 
when H1 holds (better with the larger $n$). For H1 versus H2, the coverage with $S$ = 10 is fine 
(.93 to .99). The undercoverage increases with the number of studies, because the shift of the 
bootstrap distribution adds up over the studies (see the previous section). The coverage does not 
differ between the added- and equal-evidence approach.

**Delta method (`method = "delta"`).** The delta method undercovers in many conditions (overall 
.81 for the ratios), in particular when hypotheses overlap (have the same order-restricted MLEs) 
in (some of) the studies, as expected: the differences in GORICA values are then not normally 
distributed. For example, for H1 versus the unconstrained hypothesis when H1 holds, the coverage is 
.35 to .74, and for H1 versus H2 when the parameters are in the opposite order, the CI is often 
missing (both hypotheses then have the same fit in all studies). For the weight of H1, the delta 
method performs better (about .83 to .99 per condition).

**Recommendations.**

* Keep the bootstrap as the default of `evSyn_CI()`, but note in the documentation that its CIs 
  can be (too) narrow when many studies are pooled, especially for the best hypothesis versus the 
  failsafe and when the true parameters are on the boundary of the hypotheses.
* With many studies, a centered bootstrap removes most of the undercoverage (see the previous 
  section). It could be offered as an option (or as the default for, say, $S \geq 5$), but it is 
  conservative or slightly anti-conservative in some conditions, so this choice deserves a further 
  look (e.g., a pooled version of the inversion method of `goric_CI()`).
* Use the delta method only for clearly distinguishable hypotheses (no overlap in any study).
